title: Jenkins redirects to dashboard instead of requested URL (first attempt & after session timeout)
need_summary: Whether the post-authentication redirect to the Jenkins dashboard instead of the originally requested URL is tied to redirect-safety handling in the miniOrange SAML plugin, with the maintainer pointing to `Util#isSafeToRedirectTo` and SECURITY-3501 and saying the issue was fixed in a newer plugin release.
security_topic: post-authentication redirect to original URL after SSO login
question_text:
When a user accesses a direct Jenkins resource (e.g., a job URL) and their session has expired, Jenkins correctly redirects them to authenticate via SSO. However, after successful authentication, Jenkins redirects the user to the dashboard/home page (/) instead of the originally requested URL.
This results in a poor user experience because users must manually re-navigate to the intended job.
answer_text:
This issue has already been addressed and fixed in our recent releases.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused. We kindly request that you update the plugin to the latest version and verify whether the issue is resolved.
thread_text:
ISSUE #26851: Jenkins redirects to dashboard instead of requested URL (first attempt & after session timeout)
Author: VenuReddy3129
Date: 2026-05-28T09:33:30Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
### Jenkins and plugins versions report

Jenkins incorrectly redirects users to the dashboard (/) instead of the requested job URL:

On first access to any Jenkins URL
After session timeout (~30 minutes) and re-authentication

The correct page only loads on the second attempt.

When a user accesses a direct Jenkins resource (e.g., a job URL) and their session has expired, Jenkins correctly redirects them to authenticate via SSO. However, after successful authentication, Jenkins redirects the user to the dashboard/home page (/) instead of the originally requested URL.
This results in a poor user experience because users must manually re-navigate to the intended job.

### What Operating System are you using (both controller, and any agents involved in the problem)?

Jenkins: 2.541.3
Auth: miniOrange SAML plugin (v3.4.2)
Browser: Edge
Behind reverse proxy

### Reproduction steps

Open a direct Jenkins job URL:
https://jenkins.example.com/job/sample-job/



Ensure the user session is expired:

Either wait for idle timeout (~30 minutes)
Or manually clear session cookies



The user is redirected to the SSO login page.


Complete authentication successfully.


Observe redirect behavior:

User is redirected to:
https://jenkins.example.com/

instead of:
https://jenkins.example.com/job/sample-job/





If the user again navigates to the same job URL manually, it loads correctly.

### Expected Results

After successful authentication, Jenkins should redirect the user back to the originally requested URL (e.g., /job/sample-job/), preserving user context.

### Actual Results

After authentication, Jenkins always redirects to the dashboard (/), ignoring the original request URL.

### Anything else?

_No response_

### Are you interested in contributing a fix?

_No response_

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @mawinter69 2026-05-28T11:24:07Z:
I would assume this is an issue in the mini-orange saml plugin and not a core issue. So better open bug there.
---
[c2] @daniel-beck 2026-05-28T20:03:43Z:
There's a chance this is caused by https://github.com/jenkinsci/miniorange-saml-sp-plugin/blob/c016c4cabeb94bb33f6cd1f29739617b91875483/src/main/java/org/miniorange/saml/MoSAMLAddIdp.java#L298 using `Util#isSafeToRedirectTo`, which we've progressively locked down further in the past, most recently in SECURITY-3501. Knowing what the `referer` value is would help. Another option could be that Jenkins is accessed through a URL different from the canonical configured root URL, which also opens up reverse proxy configuration as a potential source of problems.

Thank you for reaching out and for providing the detailed information regarding the issue.

We can see that you are currently using miniOrange SAML Plugin version 3.4.2, which is not the latest available version. This issue has already been addressed and fixed in our recent releases.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused. We kindly request that you update the plugin to the latest version and verify whether the issue is resolved.

If you face any issues while upgrading, or if the behavior persists even after updating to the latest version, please feel free to reach out to us at support-atlassian@miniorange.atlassian.net. You can also contact me directly at mahesh.bharti@xecurify.com, and I'll be happy to assist you further.

Looking forward to your update.

Best Regards,
Mahesh Bharti
Team miniOrange

title: Add native BeanShell scripting support to Jenkins core
need_summary: Whether native BeanShell scripting in Jenkins core would need sandboxing and be restricted so only administrators can use it, as noted in the script security discussion and the linked plugin repository.
security_topic: security restrictions for adding BeanShell scripting support in Jenkins
question_text:
### What feature do you want to see added?

Currently, Jenkins only provides native Groovy support through its Script Console and Pipeline DSL. BeanShell is a mature, actively maintained Java scripting language that offers POSIX-compatible scripting capabilities, making it a portable alternative to platform-specific scripts such as `.cmd`, `.sh` or `.ps1`.

This is not intended as a replacement for Groovy, but as a complement to it, allowing both languages to work together within the same pipeline, giving users the flexibility to leverage the strengths of each one.

Having native BeanShell support in Jenkins core would allow users to write portable build and deployment scripts that run consistently across different operating systems without requiring platform-specific interpreters, while also providing the ability to use BeanShell files (`.bsh`), allowing separation of concerns between the pipeline and the POSIX commands used, as is done with Command Scripts (`.cmd`), Bash Scripts (`.sh`) or PowerShell Scripts (`.ps1`).
answer_text: Use of that library should be restricted to controllers where every user, including every committer to every repo with a `Jenkinsfile`, is an administrator. It also doesn't support distributed builds at all.

This is not intended as a replacement for Groovy, but as a complement to it, allowing both languages to work together within the same pipeline, giving users the flexibility to leverage the strengths of each one.

Having native BeanShell support in Jenkins core would allow users to write portable build and deployment scripts that run consistently across different operating systems without requiring platform-specific interpreters, while also providing the ability to use BeanShell files (`.bsh`), allowing separation of concerns between the pipeline and the POSIX commands used, as is done with Command Scripts (`.cmd`), Bash Scripts (`.sh`) or PowerShell Scripts (`.ps1`).

### Upstream changes

_No response_

### Are you interested in contributing this feature?

I'd be willing to contribute as part of a team, though I'm a Jenkins user rather than a core developer and would need guidance on the codebase.

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @mawinter69 2026-05-24T14:20:45Z:
I don't think this is something that should be put into core.
We already have enough issues with the groovy that is bundled in core. Adding here another scripting possibility will only increase maintenance burden in core.
And integrating this into pipeline jobs anyway requires a plugin as pipeline jobs are provided by plugins.
An important thing to consider is security. I assume your intention is that such scripts run in the controller jvm. So you will need to ensure that such scripts run in a sandbox so they can only access the things they are allowed to use. So you need something similar to what script security plugin does for groovy scripts

> and Pipeline DSL

Good luck.

The Groovy Sandbox is an absolute nightmare, and the other mode of Script Security (whole-script approval) is somehow even worse.

This cannot be done in core anyway, so needs to be a plugin.

title: Offline nodes become online after config reload
need_summary: Whether Jenkins should preserve a node’s temporary offline status across reloads/restarts, with the answer anchored in the core release note and PR reference that it was fixed in Jenkins 2.548 and in core PR #26154.
security_topic: offline node status reset after Jenkins reload
question_text: I lost functionality when after jenkins reload (safeRestart/systemctl restart/by jcasc plugin - Reload existing configuration) all previously-set offline agents stay offline. On older jenkins version: Jenkins: 2.346.3 it was work that way. Offline nodes was offline until manual setting it online again. On newer version: Jenkins: 2.504.1 agents all the time(after restart/config reload) becomes online. It is bug or it was a bug before?
answer_text: It's actually in this loop https://github.com/jenkinsci/jenkins/blob/14717a3636784c756faa8aaf9101a3286892e21a/core/src/main/java/jenkins/model/Nodes.java#L118 here where the list of nodes is maintained. Here in line 124 the offline cause must be transferred from `oldNode` to `node` I think

title: Microsoft SmartScreen reports Jenkins 2.562 is an unrecognized app
need_summary: Whether Jenkins 2.562’s MSI installer warning is just SmartScreen reputation blocking and what Microsoft’s review process says about removing it, anchored by the Microsoft file-submission URL and Microsoft’s support response reference 164e4d80-22f9-4fd3-8131-2e6c8b99679f.
security_topic: SmartScreen reputation and installer trust warning
question_text: Microsoft Windows 11, Windows 2019, Windows 2022, and Windows 2025 show a SmartScreen dialog when the Jenkins 2.562 MSI installer is run.  The dialog says "Microsoft Defender SmartScreen prevented an unrecognized app from starting.  Running this app might put your PC at risk."
answer_text:
> Have we considered submitting the installer to the Microsoft Security Intelligence portal for manual review?

Thanks.  Yes, I've submitted the Jenkins 2.562 MSI file to https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/filesubmission
thread_text:
ISSUE #26716: Microsoft SmartScreen reports Jenkins 2.562 is an unrecognized app Author: MarkEWaite Date: 2026-04-28T14:36:05Z Labels: State: closed [c0] ### Jenkins and plugins versions report
Environment ```text MSI installer for Jenkins 2.562 and later ```
### What Operating System are you using (both controller, and any agents involved in the problem)? Microsoft Windows 11, Windows 2019, Windows 2022, and Windows 2025 show a SmartScreen dialog when the Jenkins 2.562 MSI installer is run. The dialog says "Microsoft Defender SmartScreen prevented an unrecognized app from starting. Running this app might put your PC at risk." ### Reproduction steps 1. When downloading the MSI installer for Jenkins 2.562 and later, Microsoft Edge may prompt that the file is infrequently downloaded. The dialog looks like this: 2. Once the "Keep anyway" button is clicked, the file downloads and can be opened 3. When the file is run, Windows displays the SmartScreen prompt that says "Microsoft Defender SmartScreen prevented an unrecognized app from starting. Running this app might put your PC at risk." The dialog looks like this: 4. When the user clicks "More info", they see a screen that confirms the install is published by "LF Open Source, LLC". That is the correct publisher and the installer is correctly signed. The dialog looks like this: 5. When the user clicks "Run anyway", the MSI installer starts and runs as expected ### Expected Results The MSI installer should not warn the user that it is infrequently downloaded or that it is an unrecognized app. ### Actual Results MSI installer reports it is infrequently downloaded and is an unknown app that might harm the PC. ### Anything else? Refer to the Jenkins Infra help desk ticket for more details: * https://github.com/jenkins-infra/helpdesk/issues/4923 ### Are you interested in contributing a fix? I plan to write a blog post and update the changelog with a banner so that users have a point of reference for the new messages. --- COMMENTS --- [c1] @Dipanshusinghh 2026-04-28T17:48:47Z: Hi @MarkEWaite 👋 I’ve reviewed this issue regarding the Microsoft SmartScreen warning for the Jenkins MSI installer. From what I understand, this is likely related to SmartScreen reputation and code-signing trust rather than a direct application bug. I’d like to contribute by helping with user-facing improvements, such as: * Adding a clear note in the changelog or documentation explaining the SmartScreen warning * Providing guidance for users on how to safely proceed with the installation * Verifying the messaging across different Windows environments for consistency If this aligns with the current direction, I’d be happy to take this up. Please let me know if I can work on it or if there’s any preferred approach. Thanks! --- [c2] @MarkEWaite 2026-04-28T18:46:32Z: @Dipanshusinghh thanks very much for your offer to help. Please install Jenkins 2.562 on as many Windows computers as you can find. We need to increase the reputation of the installer as quickly as possible so that SmartScreen will stop displaying the "Windows protected your PC" dialog. --- [c3] @MarkEWaite 2026-04-28T23:46:44Z: Several items are now available to guide administrators: * [Windows download page](https://www.jenkins.io/download/thank-you-downloading-windows-installer/) includes instructions to handle Microsoft Defender Smartscreen * [Blog post](https://www.jenkins.io/blog/2026/04/29/windows-installer-signing-change/) includes instructions for Microsoft Edge and Microsoft Defender Smartscreen, with a [community discussion thread](https://community.jenkins.io/t/windows-installer-signing-change/36842) * [Changelog](https://www.jenkins.io/changelog/2.562/) includes a brief description of Microsoft Defender Smartscreen --- [c4] @Dipanshusinghh 2026-04-29T01:26:26Z: Hi @MarkEWaite, just a thought on the ongoing SmartScreen issue—since the publisher 'LF Open Source, LLC' is now correctly identified, it's possible that the new certificate simply hasn't built enough reputation with Microsoft yet. As this is a newer release (2.562), SmartScreen often flags binaries until a certain threshold of 'clean' installs is reached globally. Have we considered submitting the installer to the Microsoft Security Intelligence portal for manual review? This can sometimes speed up the reputation-building process. --- [c5] @MarkEWaite 2026-04-29T02:01:55Z: > Have we considered submitting the installer to the Microsoft Security Intelligence portal for manual review? Thanks. Yes, I've submitted the Jenkins 2.562 MSI file to https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/filesubmission --- [c6] @MarkEWaite 2026-05-03T19:29:37Z: Microsoft responded to my submitted file. The message said: > Thank you for contacting us about https://mirror.xmission.com/jenkins/windows/2.562/jenkins.msi > If the block persists 24 hours after submission, please reply to this confirmation email to let us know the issue is not remediated. Please provide any additional details that may be relevant. This will help expedite further investigation and resolution. > > We appreciate your cooperation and patience as we work to resolve this issue. We have received the information you provided and are currently reviewing it. If it is determined that the current designation is incorrect or no longer accurate the warning will be removed. > > We typically expect to take 24 hours for our investigation. During this time, you may not see any changes to the status of your website. Please do not re-submit your request or make any changes to your website until we complete the investigation. Please note that while we review your feedback, we may not be able to respond to each submission individually. Thank you for your understanding. > > You can find additional information by reviewing the [Microsoft Defender SmartScreen Overview](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/microsoft-defender-smartscreen/microsoft-defender-smartscreen-overview). > > Thank you, > Microsoft Defender SmartScreen® Support > > Reference: 164e4d80-22f9-4fd3-8131-2e6c8b99679f --- [c7] @Dipanshusinghh 2026-05-03T19:41:23Z: Thanks for the update and for submitting the installer to Microsoft for review. In the meantime, I’ll help by installing Jenkins 2.562 across multiple Windows environments to contribute toward building SmartScreen reputation. I’ll also note any variations in the warning messages or user flow and share them here if I find anything noteworthy. When the user clicks "Run anyway", the MSI installer starts and runs as expected ### Expected Results The MSI installer should not warn the user that it is infrequently downloaded or that it is an unrecognized app. ### Actual Results MSI installer reports it is infrequently downloaded and is an unknown app that might harm the PC. ### Anything else? title: Bitbucket OAuth Plugin v0.16 broken by CHANGE-3052: access token sent via query parameter instead of Authorization header
need_summary: Whether Bitbucket OAuth Plugin v0.16 is broken because Bitbucket Cloud enforces CHANGE-3052 on access tokens in query parameters, with the issue anchored by the CHANGE-3052 announcement and the Scribe 1.3.3 signRequest behavior in OAuth20ServiceImpl.
security_topic: OAuth token transport breaking change affecting login
question_text:
The Bitbucket OAuth Plugin sends the OAuth2 access token as an access_token query string parameter instead of using the Authorization: Bearer header. This is because the plugin uses Scribe 1.3.3, whose OAuth20ServiceImpl.signRequest() method defaults to request.addQuerystringParameter(OAuthConstants.ACCESS_TOKEN, accessToken.getToken()), and the plugin's BitbucketOAuth20Service inner class in BitbucketApiV2.java does not override signRequest().
Bitbucket Cloud has announced CHANGE-3052, which deprecates passing OAuth access tokens via query parameters or POST body. Brownouts began April 20, 2026, and full enforcement is May 4, 2026, after which this plugin will be permanently broken.
answer_text:
Bitbucket oauth plugin tracks issues on Jira:
https://www.jenkins.io/participate/report-issue/redirect/#17643/bitbucket-oauth
thread_text:
ISSUE #26693: Bitbucket OAuth Plugin v0.16 broken by CHANGE-3052: access token sent via query parameter instead of Authorization header
Author: suhasrajmm
Date: 2026-04-23T11:19:37Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
### Jenkins and plugins versions report

<details>
  <summary>Environment</summary>

  <!-- Paste your environment details below -->
  ```text
  Paste the output here
  ```

</details>


### What Operating System are you using (both controller, and any agents involved in the problem)?

The Bitbucket OAuth Plugin sends the OAuth2 access token as an access_token query string parameter instead of using the Authorization: Bearer header. This is because the plugin uses Scribe 1.3.3, whose OAuth20ServiceImpl.signRequest() method defaults to request.addQuerystringParameter(OAuthConstants.ACCESS_TOKEN, accessToken.getToken()), and the plugin's BitbucketOAuth20Service inner class in BitbucketApiV2.java does not override signRequest().
Bitbucket Cloud has announced CHANGE-3052, which deprecates passing OAuth access tokens via query parameters or POST body. Brownouts began April 20, 2026, and full enforcement is May 4, 2026, after which this plugin will be permanently broken.

Affected Code
File: src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/api/BitbucketApiV2.java
The inner class BitbucketOAuth20Service (line 43) extends OAuth20ServiceImpl but does not override signRequest(). The inherited implementation sends the token as a query parameter:

// Inherited from org.scribe.oauth.OAuth20ServiceImpl (Scribe 1.3.3)
public void signRequest(Token accessToken, OAuthRequest request) {
    request.addQuerystringParameter(OAuthConstants.ACCESS_TOKEN, accessToken.getToken());
}
This causes all API calls in BitbucketApiService.java (lines 68 and 85) to send requests like:

GET https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/user?access_token=XXXXX
GET https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/user/workspaces?access_token=XXXXX
Instead of:

GET https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/user
Authorization: Bearer XXXXX

### Reproduction steps

 1.  Install Jenkins v2.516.3 (or any recent version)
 2.  Install Bitbucket OAuth Plugin v0.16
 3.  Configure Bitbucket OAuth Plugin with a valid Bitbucket OAuth consumer (Client ID and Client Secret)
 4.  Configure Jenkins to use "Bitbucket OAuth Plugin" as the Security Realm
 5.  Log out of Jenkins
 6.  Attempt to log in via Bitbucket OAuth during a CHANGE-3052 brownout window (see schedule below) or after May 4, 2026
CHANGE-3052 Brownout Schedule (UTC)

### Expected Results

•  User is successfully authenticated via Bitbucket OAuth
•  User is redirected back to Jenkins and logged in
•  Workspace roles are correctly assigned

### Actual Results

•  After Bitbucket redirects back to Jenkins (/securityRealm/finishLogin?code=...), the plugin attempts to call Bitbucket API endpoints with the access token in the query string
•  Bitbucket returns HTTP 401 during brownout windows (and permanently after May 4, 2026)
•  Jenkins displays: "Oops! A problem occurred while processing the request" with a Logging ID
•  Users are completely unable to log in to Jenkins

_No response_

title: Stashed symlink makes unstash impossible
need_summary: Whether Jenkins stash/unstash symlink handling can be safely bypassed on agents using the documented escape-hatch system properties `hudson.FilePath.ALLOW_REENTRY_PATH_TRAVERSAL` and `hudson.FilePath.ALLOW_UNTAR_SYMLINK_RESOLUTION`, as discussed in the SECURITY-3657 thread and advisory link.
security_topic: stash/unstash symlink handling after a security fix
question_text: This broke because of this security update: https://www.jenkins.io/security/advisory/2026-03-18/#SECURITY-3657
answer_text: Confirmed, setting these escape hatches for the agent process will work around the problem. Since the security fix intended to address the path traversal on the controller, this will not degrade security on most setups (hedging here only because some setups are _weird).

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @MilanTyagi2004 2026-04-01T07:08:57Z:
Hi @salomj,

I’d like to take this issue.

From what I understand, this behavior is a side-effect of the fix introduced in SECURITY-3657, where Jenkins now blocks extraction of archives if a symlink exists anywhere in the path to prevent arbitrary file write vulnerabilities .

### Problem Breakdown

* `stash` allows symlinks to be archived.
* `unstash` fails because extraction now rejects any path containing symlinks.
* This breaks valid workflows (e.g., Lerna / node_modules) where symlinks are expected and safe.

### Proposed Approach

I’m considering the following directions:

1. **Handle symlinks during stash (preferred)**

   * Detect symlinks while creating the stash archive
   * Either:

     * Skip them with a warning, or
     * Store metadata instead of raw symlinks

2. **Safe extraction validation**

   * Allow symlinks only if:

     * They resolve within the workspace
     * They don’t escape the target directory
   * This preserves security guarantees while allowing valid use cases

3. **Optional configuration (fallback)**

   * Introduce a flag like `allowSafeSymlinks`
   * Default remains secure, but users can opt-in for controlled environments

### Goal

Maintain the security guarantees introduced by SECURITY-3657 while restoring compatibility for common development workflows that rely on symlinks.

Let me know if this direction sounds good, or if you’d prefer a stricter approach (e.g., always skipping symlinks during stash).

I can start with a PR once aligned.

[c2] @daniel-beck 2026-04-01T09:42:11Z:

> Create a folder with a symlink

It's not quite as simple as that, but still too simple 😞 

```
node('a1') {
    sh 'rm -rf top/ ; mkdir -p top/sub top/sub2 ; ln -s ../sub2 top/sub/subsub ; date > top/sub2/file'
    stash includes: 'top/**', name: 'foo'
    unstash 'foo'
}
```

	at Jenkins v2.557//hudson.FilePath.readFromTar(FilePath.java:3092)
```

which seems unexpected; this may be a bug in the code for archive creation. Declaring an entry to be a symlink and then collecting its children seems wrong.

[c3] @daniel-beck 2026-04-01T10:07:25Z:
The archive code does not pass `LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS` to `Dirscanner.Glob`, so it follows symlinks -- an option the security fix does not handle well.

I see two options forward:

* Look into restricting the write-through check to only fail on symlinks leaving the root.
* (Perhaps optionally) change the behavior of stashing to not collect files through symlinks. That seems like a weird thing to do. But this could break some existing use cases that rely on symlinks to collect files to archive. OTOH, the unarchival would look really odd then it seems?

[c6] @daniel-beck 2026-04-24T09:33:38Z:
> Declaring an entry to be a symlink and then collecting its children seems wrong.

It seems this is not (exactly) what's happening here though.

```
$ tar tvzf foo.tar.gz 
-rw-r--r-- 0/0              29 2026-04-24 09:25 top/sub/subsub/file
-rw-r--r-- 0/0              29 2026-04-24 09:25 top/sub2/file
```

The `stash` tar itself only collects files. The problem is the `unstash` over a non-empty directory, because we traversed symlinks to collect files, and now want to extract them again. This also means we have (potentially significantly) inflated stash sizes, since files are potentially collected N+1 times for N symlinks.

The following Pipeline reveals the directory layout before and (when cleaning to make the `unstash` pass) after:
```
node {
    sh 'rm -rf top/ ; mkdir -p top/sub top/sub2 ; ln -s ../sub2 top/sub/subsub ; date > top/sub2/file'
    sh 'find top/ -ls'
    stash includes: 'top/**', name: 'foo'
    sh 'rm -rf top/'
    unstash 'foo'
    sh 'find top/ -ls'
}
```

comments.author: MilanTyagi2004
comments.body:
Hi @salomj,

I’d like to take this issue.

From what I understand, this behavior is a side-effect of the fix introduced in SECURITY-3657, where Jenkins now blocks extraction of archives if a symlink exists anywhere in the path to prevent arbitrary file write vulnerabilities .

### Problem Breakdown

* `stash` allows symlinks to be archived.
* `unstash` fails because extraction now rejects any path containing symlinks.
* This breaks valid workflows (e.g., Lerna / node_modules) where symlinks are expected and safe.

### Proposed Approach

I’m considering the following directions:

1. **Handle symlinks during stash (preferred)**

   * Detect symlinks while creating the stash archive
   * Either:

     * Skip them with a warning, or
     * Store metadata instead of raw symlinks

2. **Safe extraction validation**

   * Allow symlinks only if:

     * They resolve within the workspace
     * They don’t escape the target directory
   * This preserves security guarantees while allowing valid use cases

3. **Optional configuration (fallback)**

   * Introduce a flag like `allowSafeSymlinks`
   * Default remains secure, but users can opt-in for controlled environments

### Goal

Maintain the security guarantees introduced by SECURITY-3657 while restoring compatibility for common development workflows that rely on symlinks.

Let me know if this direction sounds good, or if you’d prefer a stricter approach (e.g., always skipping symlinks during stash).

I can start with a PR once aligned.

title: No longer latest versions on https://archives.jenkins.io/update-center/
need_summary: Whether Jenkins is still supposed to publish dynamic-stable update-center paths for specific LTS versions, with the answer anchored in the site layout documentation and the update site docs referenced in the thread.
security_topic: applicability of update-center path expectations for LTS versions
question_text: Expected would be that for all recent (latest) version a folder exists, like before under https://archives.jenkins.io/update-center/ as it was until /dynamic-stable-2.541.1
answer_text:
Closing as a user misunderstanding.  You've made an incorrect assumption about the contents of that directory.

The [site layout documentation](https://github.com/jenkins-infra/update-center2/blob/master/site/LAYOUT.md) does not describe any use of `dynamic-stable` and does not make any commitment that there will be a `dynamic-stable-2.541.2` to match the 2.541.2 release or the 2.541.3 release.

title: Fenced-in Admin
need_summary: Whether fencing Admin rights into limited categories is supported, with the answer anchored in Jenkins JEP 223 stating that features that cannot elevate permissions should use Overall/Manage permission.
security_topic: permission scoping and privilege escalation via admin-like features
question_text: I would like to see the ability to grant Admin rights to a user, but fence them into specific categories of configuration. For example, on a shared Jenkins site you don't want to grant Admin rights to users and risk exposing projects others should not see. But that also prevents users from creating Cloud Nodes that use Docker images as slaves.
answer_text:
This is what Overall/Manage permission is for: https://www.jenkins.io/jep/223

Anything that cannot be used to elevate one's own permission to Administer should ultimately use Manage. The problem is that many features can be used in that way. If a feature you want them "fenced in" like that can be used to elevate permissions, it's not suitable.

comments.author: Siddhartha-singh01
comments.body:
Hi, I'd like to take a look at this if no one is actively working on it.

Quick investigation in core/src/main/java/jenkins/model/run/KeepRunAction.java  the action factory does emit Keep/UnKeep entries when new-build-page.flag is enabled, gated on target.canToggleLogKeep() and target.hasPermission(Permission.UPDATE) / Permission.DELETE. My initial hypothesis is that the generic hudson.security.Permission.UPDATE / DELETE constants don't match what Run actually grants (the classic logKeep.jelly path uses Run.UPDATE), so createFor() silently returns an empty set and nothing renders in the menu  which would explain why it's missing even from the three-dot menu as the reporter mentioned.

I'll spin up a dev instance with the flag enabled to confirm the root cause before opening a PR.

@janfaracik since you own the new-build-page work, does this theory line up with what you'd expect, or is there a different reason the action isn't appearing? 

Happy to take guidance.

comments.author: mawinter69
comments.body: Afaik this is fixed since 2.556. Note that the button is now in the menu and not directly on the page anymore

comments.author: Siddhartha-singh01
comments.body:
Thanks @mawinter69  you're right, the button is back in the menu since 2.556.

One thing I noticed: KeepRunAction gates Keep/UnKeep on the generic Permission.UPDATE / Permission.DELETE (the abstract "GenericUpdate"/"GenericDelete" permissions  effectively admin-only), while sibling EditRunAction and the classic logKeep.jelly use the run-scoped Run.UPDATE / Run.DELETE. So the buttons are still hidden for users who have Run/Update + Run/Delete granted but aren't full admins. Happy to send a small follow-up PR aligning those checks  or if it's intended, I'll drop it.

Windows operating system running automated tests

```

Automated tests of symlinks should be skipped on Windows computers where symlinks are disabled:

* hudson.tasks.ArtifactArchiverTest.lengthOfArtifactIsCorrect_eventForInvalidSymlink
* hudson.tasks.ArtifactArchiverTest.outsideSymlinks

### Actual Results

Automated tests fail when symlinks are disabled:

* hudson.model.DirectoryBrowserSupportTest.symlink_avoidLeakingInformation_aboutIllegalFolder
* hudson.model.DirectoryBrowserSupportTest.symlink_insideWorkspace_areNotAllowedAnymore

### Anything else?

This is not a good first issue.

If others don't work on the issue within a few days, I'll probably work on it myself.

[c9] @jtnord 2026-01-27T16:52:20Z:
> I expect they aren't used out of choice.
> 
> Some users _may_ use them. The tests will be mostly security based tests to make sure they can't escape out of paths unintentionally.

its a developer option in windows 11, just a slide option to enable IIRC.  (or you can be old school like me and edit the group policy and create some local groups).

> Whether they are actually used in practice in Windows these days, 🤷. Could just be a case of it happens on Linux but the tests weren't marked as Linux only.
> 
> cc [@daniel-beck](https://github.com/daniel-beck) / [@Wadeck](https://github.com/Wadeck) / [@jtnord](https://github.com/jtnord) in case you have any input.

I use symlinks heavily, and a few git repos I work with have them in the repo so it's enabled at that level too!

I would be concerned if this was detected by checking if the symlink code through an exception, that is what it would likely do if it regressed so would end up with the failing code causing the tests for said failing code to self skip.  the code on windows (for junction handling which is also part of this) is very security related.

if you want to skip then using natie java code would be better than our code

```java
try {
    Files.createSymbolicLink(newLink, target);
} catch (IOException x) {
    throw new AssertionError("this should not occur!, x);
} catch (UnsupportedOperationException x) {
    throw new AssumptionError("Symbolic links are not supported on this platform - search your OS documentation for how to enable them");
}
```

> This is now failing on the Windows 2025 agents that we are using on ci.jenkins.io. Now the question is, should we ask the Jenkins infra team to enable symlinks on the Windows 2025 agents?

I see no good reason not to, I have this set locally on a group policy and a custom group.  Not sure you can enable "developer mode" on windows server so the former is probably the approach to take.

With the "developer mode" enabled, we are now able to create symlinks in pipelines with a BAT `mklink /d ...` command: https://github.com/jenkins-infra/helpdesk/issues/4972#issuecomment-3806413876

Does it fix the builds here?

title: Race condition in HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm.doCreateFirstAccount allows multiple initial admin accounts
need_summary: Whether the reported race condition in HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm.doCreateFirstAccount can create multiple initial admin accounts, and the answer rests on the linked PR https://github.com/jenkinsci/jenkins/pull/26036 and the synchronized lock code it proposes.
security_topic: race condition in initial admin account creation
question_text: A race condition exists in `HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm.doCreateFirstAccount`. The `hasSomeUser()` check is non-atomic and unsynchronized. In testing with 20 concurrent threads, 20 different user accounts were created, and all 20 were granted administrative privileges via `tryToMakeAdmin(u)`.
answer_text:
I opened a PR that makes the first account creation atomic by synchronizing the check and creation logic on a dedicated lock, ensuring that only one initial admin user can be created:

https://github.com/jenkinsci/jenkins/pull/26036
thread_text:
ISSUE #26027: Race condition in HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm.doCreateFirstAccount allows multiple initial admin accounts Author: geeknik Date: 2026-01-02T05:19:44Z Labels: State: closed [c0] ### Jenkins and plugins versions report
Environment Jenkins: 2.545-SNAPSHOT OS: Linux - 6.12.11-200.fc41.x86_64 Java: 25.0.1 - Red Hat, Inc. (OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM) --- antisamy-markup-formatter:173.v680e3a_b_69ff3 asm-api:9.9-185.va_6c6b_3348b_c3 bootstrap5-api:5.3.8-895.v4d0d8e47fea_d bouncycastle-api:2.30.1.82-277.v70ca_0b_877184 caffeine-api:3.2.3-194.v31a_b_f7a_b_5a_81 checks-api:373.vfe7645102093 cloudbees-folder:6.1073.va_7888eb_dd514 commons-lang3-api:3.20.0-109.ve43756e2d2b_4 commons-text-api:1.15.0-210.v7480a_da_70b_9e credentials:1453.v9b_a_29777a_b_fd display-url-api:2.217.va_6b_de84cc74b_ echarts-api:6.0.0-1165.vd1283a_3e37d4 font-awesome-api:7.1.0-882.v1dfb_771e3278 instance-identity:203.v15e81a_1b_7a_38 ionicons-api:94.vcc3065403257 jackson2-api:2.19.2-408.v18248a_324cfe jquery3-api:3.7.1-594.vb_3864f326cf0 junit:1380.v491ff054cd35 mailer:525.v2458b_d8a_1a_71 matrix-auth:3.2.9 matrix-project:870.v9db_fcfc2f45b_ plugin-util-api:6.1192.v30fe6e2837ff prism-api:1.30.0-630.va_e19d17f83b_0 scm-api:724.v7d839074eb_5c script-security:1385.v7d2d9ec4d909 structs:362.va_b_695ef4fdf9 variant:70.va_d9f17f859e0 workflow-api:1398.v67030756d3fb_ workflow-step-api:710.v3e456cc85233 workflow-support:1010.vb_b_39488a_9841
### What Operating System are you using (both controller, and any agents involved in the problem)? Fedora 43 ### Reproduction steps 1. Initialize a clean Jenkins installation using `HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm` as the security realm. 2. Ensure no user accounts have been created yet (initial setup state). 3. Simultaneously send multiple concurrent POST requests to the `/securityRealm/createFirstAccount` endpoint with different usernames and valid account details. 4. Verify the number of users created and their permissions. ### Expected Results Only the very first request should succeed in creating an account. All subsequent concurrent requests should fail with a 401 Unauthorized error (or similar) because a user already exists or is being created, preventing the creation of multiple initial administrator accounts. ### Actual Results A race condition exists in `HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm.doCreateFirstAccount`. The `hasSomeUser()` check is non-atomic and unsynchronized. In testing with 20 concurrent threads, 20 different user accounts were created, and all 20 were granted administrative privileges via `tryToMakeAdmin(u)`. ### Anything else? The vulnerability is a classic Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use race condition in `core/src/main/java/hudson/security/HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm.java` between lines 366-376. While impact is limited to the initial setup phase, it allows an attacker to gain admin access if they can time requests during the window before the first user is fully persisted. ### Are you interested in contributing a fix? Yes, the fix involves adding a static lock object to synchronize the `doCreateFirstAccount` method. This ensures the `hasSomeUser()` check and subsequent user creation are atomic. --- COMMENTS --- [c1] @Pnkcaht 2026-01-03T02:26:16Z: Hi, I was able to reproduce the issue during the initial setup by sending multiple concurrent POST requests to `/securityRealm/createFirstAccount`. The method `doCreateFirstAccount` checks `hasSomeUser()` and then creates the user without any synchronization, which allows a race condition where multiple requests can pass the check before the first user is persisted. I opened a PR that makes the first account creation atomic by synchronizing the check and creation logic on a dedicated lock, ensuring that only one initial admin user can be created: https://github.com/jenkinsci/jenkins/pull/26036 ```java /** * Lock used to make initial admin account creation atomic. */ private static final Object CREATE_FIRST_ACCOUNT_LOCK = new Object(); /** * Creates a first admin user account. * *

* This can be run by anyone, but only to create the very first user account. */ @RequirePOST public void doCreateFirstAccount(StaplerRequest2 req, StaplerResponse2 rsp) throws IOException, ServletException { synchronized (CREATE_FIRST_ACCOUNT_LOCK) { if (hasSomeUser()) { rsp.sendError(SC_UNAUTHORIZED, "First user was already created"); return; } User u = createAccount(req, rsp, false, "firstUser.jelly"); if (u != null) { tryToMakeAdmin(u); loginAndTakeBack(req, rsp, u); } } } ``` --- [c2] @daniel-beck 2026-01-03T12:37:14Z: > The vulnerability I do not consider this to be a vulnerability, since the user was clearly entitled to perform the action. They could just run a Groovy script instead. The outcome (multiple admin users) might be surprising, but it's unlikely to occur. Realistically, the current approach going from no users to having the Jenkins security realm set up is a little awkward. Note that, if this were a vulnerability, this wouldn't be the place to report it. ---

### What Operating System are you using (both controller, and any agents involved in the problem)?

Fedora 43

### Reproduction steps

   1. Initialize a clean Jenkins installation using `HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm` as the security realm.
   2. Ensure no user accounts have been created yet (initial setup state).
   3. Simultaneously send multiple concurrent POST requests to the `/securityRealm/createFirstAccount` endpoint with different usernames and valid account details.
   4. Verify the number of users created and their permissions.


### Expected Results

Only the very first request should succeed in creating an account. All subsequent concurrent requests should fail with a 401 Unauthorized error (or similar) because a user already exists or is being created, preventing the creation of multiple initial administrator accounts.

### Actual Results

A race condition exists in `HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm.doCreateFirstAccount`. The `hasSomeUser()` check is non-atomic and unsynchronized. In testing with 20 concurrent threads, 20 different user accounts were created, and all 20 were granted administrative privileges via `tryToMakeAdmin(u)`.

### Anything else?

The vulnerability is a classic Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use race condition in `core/src/main/java/hudson/security/HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm.java` between lines 366-376. While impact is limited to the initial setup phase, it allows an attacker to gain admin access if they can time requests during the window before the first user is fully persisted.

### Are you interested in contributing a fix?

Yes, the fix involves adding a static lock object to synchronize the `doCreateFirstAccount` method. This ensures the `hasSomeUser()` check and subsequent user creation are atomic.

I do not consider this to be a vulnerability, since the user was clearly entitled to perform the action. They could just run a Groovy script instead. The outcome (multiple admin users) might be surprising, but it's unlikely to occur. title: Form is larger than max length 200000
need_summary: Whether Jenkins 2.538’s Jetty 12.1 form-size limit caused the save failure and that the workaround is to set `--requestFormContentSize=3000000`, based on the Jetty form-size documentation and PR 12718.
security_topic: request form size limit causing job-save failure
question_text: The error is triggered because of the size of the Execute shell command. With 71029 chars in there is triggers the error.
answer_text:
> You should be able to workaround your problem by setting `requestFormContentSize` to a large value

You're right!  Thanks!  The online help for `java -jar jenkins.war --help` does not mention `--requestFormContentSize` as an accepted argument, but it works.  I confirmed it works with the command line:

`java -jar jenkins.war --requestFormContentSize=3000000`

I confirmed it fails with the command line:

`java -jar jenkins.war --requestFormContentSize=-1`

I can duplicate the issue if I create a freestyle project with your list of plugins and paste the complete text of ["A Christmas Carol"](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/46/pg46.txt) into the Execute shell step. Jenkins 2.531 accepts that large amount of text, while Jenkins 2.538 and 2.542 do not. Jenkins 2.531 bundles winstone 8.13.1 with Eclipse Jetty 12.0.25. comments.author: mawinter69
comments.body:
hmm, actually by default the form contentsize is not limited in winstone.
See https://github.com/jenkinsci/winstone/blob/b51575433e8ad9e01d47fb23b339fe760d14c0d7/src/main/java/winstone/cmdline/Option.java#L100 and https://github.com/jenkinsci/winstone/blob/b51575433e8ad9e01d47fb23b339fe760d14c0d7/src/main/java/winstone/HostConfiguration.java#L179

So you should check whether you set the option `requestFormContentSize` when starting Jenkins. If yes either remove that or increase it.

comments.author: maxdegraaf
comments.body: The requestFormContentSize is not used. Running 2.531 there were no issue and it start failing now we are running 2.538.

comments.author: MarkEWaite
comments.body:
Thanks for the report.  I can duplicate the issue if I create a freestyle project with your list of plugins and paste the complete text of ["A Christmas Carol"](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/46/pg46.txt) into the Execute shell step.  Jenkins 2.531 accepts that large amount of text, while Jenkins 2.538 and 2.542 do not.

Jenkins 2.531 bundles winstone 8.13.1 with Eclipse Jetty 12.0.25.  Jenkins 2.538 bundles winstone 8.1023.v8b_42b_1b_79b_f7 with Eclipse Jetty 12.1.4.

I'm able to avoid the issue by running Jenkins with the command:

```
java -Dorg.eclipse.jetty.server.Request.maxFormContentSize=3000000 -jar jenkins.war
```

In case you're interested, there are issues with several of the plugins installed on your controller.  Those plugins don't affect this issue, but they may affect the long term health of your Jenkins controller.

I had to disable the Atlassian Bitbucket integration plugin in order to see the failure.

There are many plugins in your plugin list that are deprecated or no longer useful.  They should be removed.  The message says:

The following installed plugins are deprecated:

* [Cobertura Plugin](https://plugins.jenkins.io/cobertura)
* [Code Coverage Plugin](https://plugins.jenkins.io/code-coverage-api)
* [Green Balls](https://github.com/jenkins-infra/update-center2/pull/735)
* [JavaScript GUI Lib: ACE Editor bundle plugin](https://github.com/jenkins-infra/update-center2/pull/857)
* [JavaScript GUI Lib: Handlebars bundle plugin](https://github.com/jenkins-infra/update-center2/pull/857)
* [JavaScript GUI Lib: Moment.js bundle plugin](https://github.com/jenkins-infra/update-center2/pull/857)
* [JavaScript GUI Lib: jQuery bundles (jQuery and jQuery UI) plugin](https://plugins.jenkins.io/jquery-detached)
* [Multiple SCMs plugin](https://plugins.jenkins.io/multiple-scms)
* [jQuery UI plugin](https://plugins.jenkins.io/jquery-ui)

Your set of plugins includes several authentication plugins.  Only one of them can be active at a time.  The others can be removed.  For example, you probably only need one of the following plugins:

* PAM Authentication plugin
* Active Directory plugin
* LDAP Plugin
* SAML Plugin

comments.author: MarkEWaite
comments.body:
I've uploaded a minimal reproduction case that can be run from a Linux shell with the command `bash ./README`.  Steps to duplicate the issue:

1. Unpack the zip file [jenkins-25958.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24271916/jenkins-25958.zip)
2. Change to the `jenkins-25958` directory
3. Start the controller with `bash ./README`
4. Login to the controller with your Linux username and the password the same as the username
5. Edit the job named `large-execute-shell-step` from a web browser
6. Make any change to the job and save the change in order to see the failure

comments.author: MarkEWaite
comments.body:
@olamy this seems to be a change in behavior between Jetty 12.0 and Jetty 12.1.  I think that we'll want to make a change in winstone to adapt to this change in Jetty.  I think that we'll need to backport it to the Jenkins 2.541.1 LTS in time for the LTS release candidate Jan 7, 2026.

If you're available to help with understanding what changed between Jetty 12.0 and Jetty 12.1 with regard to `org.eclipse.jetty.server.Request.maxFormContentSize`, that would be great.  The [Jetty 12.1.x documentation page](https://github.com/jetty/jetty.project/blob/jetty-12.1.x/documentation/jetty/modules/programming-guide/pages/security/configuring-form-size.adoc) on form size was updated in January of this year for the Jetty 12.1 releases.

comments.author: mawinter69
comments.body:
Caused by https://github.com/jetty/jetty.project/pull/12718
This actually makes `-1` to use the default and is not setting it to unlimited anymore.

comments.author: maxdegraaf
comments.body: Thanks guys for looking into this. And i will check those plugins. Some are depricated but still in use. Thanks again.

comments.author: MarkEWaite
comments.body:
> You should be able to workaround your problem by setting `requestFormContentSize` to a large value

You're right!  Thanks!  The online help for `java -jar jenkins.war --help` does not mention `--requestFormContentSize` as an accepted argument, but it works.  I confirmed it works with the command line:

`java -jar jenkins.war --requestFormContentSize=3000000`

I confirmed it fails with the command line:

`java -jar jenkins.war --requestFormContentSize=-1`

comments.author: MarkEWaite
comments.body: Reopened the issue because a new release of winstone needs to be created and included in Jenkins core.

comments.author: daniel-beck
comments.body:
@timja Thanks.

This seems to be due to https://github.com/KostyaSha/github-integration-plugin/blob/358149f481dc8735c89d099da451af8903049f3d/github-pullrequest-plugin/src/main/resources/org/jenkinsci/plugins/github/pullrequest/GitHubPRRepository/index.groovy#L41 if Content Security Policy is being enforced. Disable CSP enforcement again for now, you're using a plugin not yet compatible (and already known to not be compatible).

Docs, just in case: https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/security/csp/

As the plugin tracks issues outside the `jenkinsci` org, I'm closing this one.

comments.author: daniel-beck
comments.body:
> I don't see anything suspicious in logs or developer console

Weird though, that should complain about inline JS being prohibited when you load the page. Look for mentions of `script-src` and/or `unsafe-inline`.

comments.author: cocorossello
comments.body:
Sorry, you are right. There are warnings when the page is rendered, I only looked for warnings when clicking the button. 

I can confirm that disabling CSP works, thanks for the explanation

comments.author: daniel-beck
comments.body:
https://github.com/KostyaSha/github-integration-plugin/releases/tag/0.7.3 should allow you to re-enable CSP enforcement.

(Make sure to check the rest of the plugins for compatibility though 😉)

title: Exceptions in console with build cause being time-based trigger
need_summary: The thread asks whether a Jenkins build cause deserialization bug can crash build-page/script-console cause handling, and the concrete anchor is the maintainer-cited reproduction in comments plus the referenced issue #26392 and the build.xml snippet showing a null upstream cause field.
security_topic: null cause field leading to console/view exceptions
question_text:
For script console:

```groovy
build = Jenkins.getInstance().getItem('build').getBuild('1337')
println(build.getCauses())
println(build.getCause())
```

For view:

```text
WARNING	h.ExpressionFactory2$JexlExpression#evaluate: Caught exception evaluating: it.causeCounts in /view/VIEW/job/build/1337/. Reason: java.lang.reflect.InvocationTargetException
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.util.Map.getClass()" because "m" is null
...
```

What is causing this error and is it related to the time-based trigger / upstream build cause?
answer_text: Seems the field introduced in #26392 can be null sometimes. It seems to work fine for a build that I just started, but not for an older build (so maybe serialization+deserialization round trip causes the problem).

title: Jenkins redirects to dashboard instead of requested URL (first attempt & after session timeout)
need_summary: Whether the redirect-to-dashboard behavior after SSO re-authentication is a security-related redirect issue, with the answer anchored by the miniOrange maintainer saying it was fixed in a later plugin release.
security_topic: post-authentication redirect to requested URL
question_text:
When a user accesses a direct Jenkins resource (e.g., a job URL) and their session has expired, Jenkins correctly redirects them to authenticate via SSO. However, after successful authentication, Jenkins redirects them to the dashboard/home page (/) instead of the originally requested URL.
This results in a poor user experience because users must manually re-navigate to the intended job.

### Expected Results

After successful authentication, Jenkins should redirect the user back to the originally requested URL (e.g., /job/sample-job/), preserving user context.
answer_text:
Hi @VenuReddy3129 ,

Thank you for reaching out and for providing the detailed information regarding the issue.

We can see that you are currently using miniOrange SAML Plugin version 3.4.2, which is not the latest available version. This issue has already been addressed and fixed in our recent releases.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused. We kindly request that you update the plugin to the latest version and verify whether the issue is resolved.

If you face any issues while upgrading, or if the behavior persists even after updating to the latest version, please feel free to reach out to us at support-atlassian@miniorange.atlassian.net. You can also contact me directly at mahesh.bharti@xecurify.com, and I'll be happy to assist you further.

Looking forward to your update.

Best Regards,
Mahesh Bharti
Team miniOrange

Author: VenuReddy3129
Date: 2026-05-28T09:33:30Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
### Jenkins and plugins versions report

Jenkins incorrectly redirects users to the dashboard (/) instead of the requested job URL:

On first access to any Jenkins URL
After session timeout (~30 minutes) and re-authentication

The correct page only loads on the second attempt.

When a user accesses a direct Jenkins resource (e.g., a job URL) and their session has expired, Jenkins correctly redirects them to authenticate via SSO. However, after successful authentication, Jenkins redirects the user to the dashboard/home page (/) instead of the originally requested URL.
This results in a poor user experience because users must manually re-navigate to the intended job.

### What Operating System are you using (both controller, and any agents involved in the problem)?

Jenkins: 2.541.3
Auth: miniOrange SAML plugin (v3.4.2)
Browser: Edge
Behind reverse proxy

### Reproduction steps

Open a direct Jenkins job URL:
https://jenkins.example.com/job/sample-job/



Ensure the user session is expired:

Either wait for idle timeout (~30 minutes)
Or manually clear session cookies



The user is redirected to the SSO login page.


Complete authentication successfully.


Observe redirect behavior:

User is redirected to:
https://jenkins.example.com/

instead of:
https://jenkins.example.com/job/sample-job/





If the user again navigates to the same job URL manually, it loads correctly.

### Expected Results

After successful authentication, Jenkins should redirect the user back to the originally requested URL (e.g., /job/sample-job/), preserving user context.

### Actual Results

After authentication, Jenkins always redirects to the dashboard (/), ignoring the original request URL.

### Anything else?

_No response_

### Are you interested in contributing a fix?

_No response_

I would assume this is an issue in the mini-orange saml plugin and not a core issue. So better open bug there.

title: Add native BeanShell scripting support to Jenkins core
need_summary: Whether a BeanShell scripting plugin would be safe to use only on Jenkins controllers where every user and every Jenkinsfile committer is an administrator, based on Daniel Beck’s restriction in comment c4.
security_topic: sandboxing and access control for scripting in Jenkins core
question_text:
### What feature do you want to see added?

Currently, Jenkins only provides native Groovy support through its Script Console and Pipeline DSL. BeanShell is a mature, actively maintained Java scripting language that offers POSIX-compatible scripting capabilities, making it a portable alternative to platform-specific scripts such as `.cmd`, `.sh` or `.ps1`.

This is not intended as a replacement for Groovy, but as a complement to it, allowing both languages to work together within the same pipeline, giving users the flexibility to leverage the strengths of each one.

Having native BeanShell support in Jenkins core would allow users to write portable build and deployment scripts that run consistently across different operating systems without requiring platform-specific interpreters, while also providing the ability to use BeanShell files (`.bsh`), allowing separation of concerns between the pipeline and the POSIX commands used, as is done with Command Scripts (`.cmd`), Bash Scripts (`.sh`) or PowerShell Scripts (`.ps1`).
answer_text: Use of that library should be restricted to controllers where every user, including every committer to every repo with a `Jenkinsfile`, is an administrator. It also doesn't support distributed builds at all.

[c1] @mawinter69 2026-05-24T14:20:45Z:
I don't think this is something that should be put into core.
We already have enough issues with the groovy that is bundled in core. Adding here another scripting possibility will only increase maintenance burden in core.
And integrating this into pipeline jobs anyway requires a plugin as pipeline jobs are provided by plugins.
An important thing to consider is security. I assume your intention is that such scripts run in the controller jvm. So you will need to ensure that such scripts run in a sandbox so they can only access the things they are allowed to use. So you need something similar to what script security plugin does for groovy scripts

security_topic: applicability of a symlink/path-traversal security fix to stash/unstash
question_text: This broke because of this security update: https://www.jenkins.io/security/advisory/2026-03-18/#SECURITY-3657

ISSUE #26563: Stashed symlink makes unstash impossible
Author: salomj
Date: 2026-03-31T19:30:50Z
Labels: regression, 2.555.3-fixed
State: closed

[c0]
### Jenkins and plugins versions report
<details>
  <summary>Environment</summary>

  ```text
Jenkins: v2.541.3
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
Java: openjdk version "21.0.10" 2026-01-20
  ```

</details>


### What Operating System are you using (both controller, and any agents involved in the problem)?

<details>
  <summary>cat /etc/os-release</summary>

  ```text
PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS"
NAME="Ubuntu"
VERSION_ID="22.04"

openjdk version "21.0.10" 2026-01-20
OpenJDK Runtime Environment (build 21.0.10+7-Ubuntu-122.04)
OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM (build 21.0.10+7-Ubuntu-122.04, mixed mode, sharing)
  ```

</details>

### Reproduction steps

1. Create a folder with a symlink
2. Stash the symlink
3. Unstash

This occurs in our node projects which use lerna, as lerna refers to other packages in the project utilizing symlinks in the `node_modules` folder. We stash the `node_modules` folder in order to speed up the builds.

### Expected Results

Either of the following:

1. Stash should not be able to stash symlinks. 
    - Maybe provide a warning and ignore symlinks.
2. Unstash of symlinks is allowed
    - Maybe rework Stash to not have an archive with the security vulnerability.
    - Maybe verify that the symlinks don't have the security vulnerability when extracted.
    - Maybe allow archives to extract symlinks in archives that were created by Jenkins and known to not have symlinks with the security vulnerability.

### Actual Results

An exception is thrown: identifying content removed and surrounded in `<>`.
```
java.io.IOException: Tar install.tar.gz attempts to write to file with symlink in path: node_modules/<path/to/other/lerna/package>/CHANGELOG.md
	at Jenkins v2.541.3//hudson.FilePath.readFromTar(FilePath.java:3092)
Also:   hudson.remoting.Channel$CallSiteStackTrace: Remote call to <agent.server.address>
		at hudson.remoting.Channel.attachCallSiteStackTrace(Channel.java:1916)

		at hudson.FilePath.act(FilePath.java:1217)
		at hudson.FilePath.act(FilePath.java:1206)
		at hudson.FilePath.untar(FilePath.java:618)
		at PluginClassLoader for workflow-api//org.jenkinsci.plugins.workflow.flow.StashManager.unstash(StashManager.java:162)
		at PluginClassLoader for workflow-basic-steps//org.jenkinsci.plugins.workflow.support.steps.stash.UnstashStep$Execution.run(UnstashStep.java:78)
		at PluginClassLoader for workflow-basic-steps//org.jenkinsci.plugins.workflow.support.steps.stash.UnstashStep$Execution.run(UnstashStep.java:65)
		at PluginClassLoader for workflow-step-api//org.jenkinsci.plugins.workflow.steps.SynchronousNonBlockingStepExecution.lambda$start$0(SynchronousNonBlockingStepExecution.java:49)
		at java.base/java.util.concurrent.Executors$RunnableAdapter.call(Executors.java:572)
Also:   org.jenkinsci.plugins.workflow.actions.ErrorAction$ErrorId: 0bebd5c1-5087-422b-9669-135ed238a3ad
Caused: java.io.IOException: Failed to extract install.tar.gz
	at Jenkins v2.541.3//hudson.FilePath.readFromTar(FilePath.java:3121)
	at Jenkins v2.541.3//hudson.FilePath.readFromTar(FilePath.java:3057)
	at Jenkins v2.541.3//hudson.FilePath$UntarRemote.invoke(FilePath.java:637)
	at Jenkins v2.541.3//hudson.FilePath$UntarRemote.invoke(FilePath.java:624)
	at Jenkins v2.541.3//hudson.FilePath$FileCallableWrapper.call(FilePath.java:3631)
	at hudson.remoting.UserRequest.perform(UserRequest.java:225)
	at hudson.remoting.UserRequest.perform(UserRequest.java:50)
	at hudson.remoting.Request$2.run(Request.java:391)
	at hudson.remoting.InterceptingExecutorService.lambda$wrap$0(InterceptingExecutorService.java:81)
	at java.base/java.util.concurrent.FutureTask.run(FutureTask.java:317)

	at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:642)

### Anything else?

This broke because of this security update: https://www.jenkins.io/security/advisory/2026-03-18/#SECURITY-3657

### Are you interested in contributing a fix?

_No response_

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @MilanTyagi2004 2026-04-01T07:08:57Z:
Hi @salomj,

I’d like to take this issue.

From what I understand, this behavior is a side-effect of the fix introduced in SECURITY-3657, where Jenkins now blocks extraction of archives if a symlink exists anywhere in the path to prevent arbitrary file write vulnerabilities .

### Problem Breakdown

* `stash` allows symlinks to be archived.
* `unstash` fails because extraction now rejects any path containing symlinks.
* This breaks valid workflows (e.g., Lerna / node_modules) where symlinks are expected and safe.

### Proposed Approach

I’m considering the following directions:

1. **Handle symlinks during stash (preferred)**

   * Detect symlinks while creating the stash archive
   * Either:

     * Skip them with a warning, or
     * Store metadata instead of raw symlinks

2. **Safe extraction validation**

   * Allow symlinks only if:

     * They resolve within the workspace
     * They don’t escape the target directory
   * This preserves security guarantees while allowing valid use cases

3. **Optional configuration (fallback)**

   * Introduce a flag like `allowSafeSymlinks`
   * Default remains secure, but users can opt-in for controlled environments

### Goal

Maintain the security guarantees introduced by SECURITY-3657 while restoring compatibility for common development workflows that rely on symlinks.

Let me know if this direction sounds good, or if you’d prefer a stricter approach (e.g., always skipping symlinks during stash).

I can start with a PR once aligned.

---
[c2] @daniel-beck 2026-04-01T09:42:11Z:
Thanks for your report.

> Create a folder with a symlink
> Stash the symlink
> Unstash

It's not quite as simple as that, but still too simple 😞 

```
node('a1') {
    sh 'rm -rf top/ ; mkdir -p top/sub top/sub2 ; ln -s ../sub2 top/sub/subsub ; date > top/sub2/file'
    stash includes: 'top/**', name: 'foo'
    unstash 'foo'
}
```
causes
```
java.io.IOException: Tar foo.tar.gz attempts to write to file with symlink in path: top/sub/subsub/file
	at Jenkins v2.557//hudson.FilePath.readFromTar(FilePath.java:3092)
```

which seems unexpected; this may be a bug in the code for archive creation. Declaring an entry to be a symlink and then collecting its children seems wrong.
---
[c3] @daniel-beck 2026-04-01T10:07:25Z:
The archive code does not pass `LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS` to `Dirscanner.Glob`, so it follows symlinks -- an option the security fix does not handle well.

I see two options forward:

* Look into restricting the write-through check to only fail on symlinks leaving the root.
* (Perhaps optionally) change the behavior of stashing to not collect files through symlinks. That seems like a weird thing to do. But this could break some existing use cases that rely on symlinks to collect files to archive. OTOH, the unarchival would look really odd then it seems?
---
[c4] @timja 2026-04-01T10:15:36Z:
1. Look into restricting the write-through check to only fail on symlinks leaving the root.
Seems sensible.

2. change the behavior of stashing to not collect files through symlinks
Agreed that it sounds sensible but is more risky if people are depending on that.
---
[c5] @salomj 2026-04-01T21:21:56Z:
> 2. **Safe extraction validation**
>    
>    * Allow symlinks only if:
>      
>      * They resolve within the workspace
>      * They don’t escape the target directory
>    * This preserves security guarantees while allowing valid use cases

I believe this to be the ideal approach, but I'm willing to accept any solution that doesn't break `unstash`.


---
[c6] @daniel-beck 2026-04-24T09:33:38Z:
> Declaring an entry to be a symlink and then collecting its children seems wrong.

It seems this is not (exactly) what's happening here though.

```
$ tar tvzf foo.tar.gz 
-rw-r--r-- 0/0              29 2026-04-24 09:25 top/sub/subsub/file
-rw-r--r-- 0/0              29 2026-04-24 09:25 top/sub2/file
```

The `stash` tar itself only collects files. The problem is the `unstash` over a non-empty directory, because we traversed symlinks to collect files, and now want to extract them again. This also means we have (potentially significantly) inflated stash sizes, since files are potentially collected N+1 times for N symlinks.

The following Pipeline reveals the directory layout before and (when cleaning to make the `unstash` pass) after:
```
node {
    sh 'rm -rf top/ ; mkdir -p top/sub top/sub2 ; ln -s ../sub2 top/sub/subsub ; date > top/sub2/file'
    sh 'find top/ -ls'
    stash includes: 'top/**', name: 'foo'
    sh 'rm -rf top/'
    unstash 'foo'
    sh 'find top/ -ls'
}
```
Output:
```
[Pipeline] Start of Pipeline
[Pipeline] node
Running on [Jenkins](http://localhost:8080/computer/(built-in)/) in /var/jenkins_home/workspace/pl
[Pipeline] {
[Pipeline] sh
+ rm -rf top/
+ mkdir -p top/sub top/sub2
+ ln -s ../sub2 top/sub/subsub
+ date
[Pipeline] sh
+ find top/ -ls
  7675063      4 drwxr-xr-x   4 jenkins  jenkins      4096 Apr 24 09:28 top/
  7675070      4 drwxr-xr-x   2 jenkins  jenkins      4096 Apr 24 09:28 top/sub
  7675066      0 lrwxrwxrwx   1 jenkins  jenkins         7 Apr 24 09:28 top/sub/subsub -> ../sub2
  7675073      4 drwxr-xr-x   2 jenkins  jenkins      4096 Apr 24 09:28 top/sub2
  7675079      4 -rw-r--r--   1 jenkins  jenkins        29 Apr 24 09:28 top/sub2/file
[Pipeline] stash
Stashed 2 file(s)
[Pipeline] sh
+ rm -rf top/
[Pipeline] unstash
[Pipeline] sh
+ find top/ -ls
  7675073      4 drwxr-xr-x   4 jenkins  jenkins      4096 Apr 24 09:28 top/
  7675079      4 drwxr-xr-x   3 jenkins  jenkins      4096 Apr 24 09:28 top/sub
  7675080      4 drwxr-xr-x   2 jenkins  jenkins      4096 Apr 24 09:28 top/sub/subsub
  7675083      4 -rw-r--r--   1 jenkins  jenkins        29 Apr 24 09:28 top/sub/subsub/file
  7675084      4 drwxr-xr-x   2 jenkins  jenkins      4096 Apr 24 09:28 top/sub2
  7675070      4 -rw-r--r--   1 jenkins  jenkins        29 Apr 24 09:28 top/sub2/file
[Pipeline] }
[Pipeline] // node
[Pipeline] End of Pipeline
Finished: SUCCESS
```

A fix in core to be more permissive with symlinks would retain the original symlink and write to the same physical file twice, but at least the pre-linked directory layout should remain the same.

OTOH there's definitely a problem with `unstash` potentially resulting in completely different directory layouts than would be expected. Not following symlinks, and collecting symlinks and files should largely result in a correct `unstash` (except for empty directories).
---
[c7] @daniel-beck 2026-04-24T09:58:36Z:
<s>Unless we start tracking which symbolic links were created during extraction vs. which are pre-existing,</s>* I expect some unstashes to still fail: Those that traverse symlinks outside the base directory. Example failing Pipeline:
```
node {
    sh 'rm -rf *'
    sh 'mkdir -p foo bar ; ln -s ../bar foo/bar ; date > bar/file'
    dir ('foo') {
        stash includes: '**', name: 'foo'
        unstash 'foo'
    }
}
```

Resulting workspace layout:
```
find . -ls
  7675052      4 drwxr-xr-x   5 jenkins  jenkins      4096 Apr 24 09:55 .
  7675093      4 drwxr-xr-x   2 jenkins  jenkins      4096 Apr 24 09:55 ./bar
  7675095      4 -rw-r--r--   1 jenkins  jenkins        29 Apr 24 09:55 ./bar/file
  7675090      4 drwxr-xr-x   2 jenkins  jenkins      4096 Apr 24 09:55 ./foo
  7675094      0 lrwxrwxrwx   1 jenkins  jenkins         6 Apr 24 09:55 ./foo/bar -> ../bar
```

Resulting stash:
```
$ tar tvzf foo.tar.gz 
-rw-r--r-- 0/0              29 2026-04-24 09:55 bar/file
```

Build log:
```
java.io.IOException: Tar foo.tar.gz attempts to write to file with symlink in path: bar/file
	at hudson.FilePath.readFromTar(FilePath.java:3092)
Also:   org.jenkinsci.plugins.workflow.actions.ErrorAction$ErrorId: db7a564e-2e7a-41aa-98c4-8ff2e04f7593
Caused: java.io.IOException: Failed to extract foo.tar.gz
	at hudson.FilePath.readFromTar(FilePath.java:3121)
	at hudson.FilePath.readFromTar(FilePath.java:3057)
```

The pre-existing symlink `foo/bar` escapes the `unstash` base dir `foo/`, so `bar/file` will be rejected.


*: That won't work, because then repeated `archiveArtifacts` calls will be allowed to escape.
---
[c8] @daniel-beck 2026-04-24T10:02:44Z:
Another option could be to only apply these protections on the controller (`JenkinsJVM#isJenkinsJVM`).

That would still fail `unstash` on the built-in node, but at least users with agents would not have this problem.
---
[c9] @daniel-beck 2026-04-24T14:06:40Z:
> Another option could be to only apply these protections on the controller (`JenkinsJVM#isJenkinsJVM`).

This is basically what @jglick proposed in https://github.com/jenkinsci/jenkins/pull/5886. Instead I ended up going with another approach that relaxed the canonicalization behavior due to some poor assumptions about the attack vector, and made it easier to have path traversal (although didn't introduce it then; some of the issues SECURITY-3657 fixed existed before).
---
[c10] @jglick 2026-04-24T17:37:21Z:

comments.author: MilanTyagi2004
comments.body:
Hi @salomj,

I’d like to take this issue.

From what I understand, this behavior is a side-effect of the fix introduced in SECURITY-3657, where Jenkins now blocks extraction of archives if a symlink exists anywhere in the path to prevent arbitrary file write vulnerabilities .

### Problem Breakdown

* `stash` allows symlinks to be archived.
* `unstash` fails because extraction now rejects any path containing symlinks.
* This breaks valid workflows (e.g., Lerna / node_modules) where symlinks are expected and safe.

### Proposed Approach

I’m considering the following directions:

1. **Handle symlinks during stash (preferred)**

   * Detect symlinks while creating the stash archive
   * Either:

     * Skip them with a warning, or
     * Store metadata instead of raw symlinks

2. **Safe extraction validation**

   * Allow symlinks only if:

     * They resolve within the workspace
     * They don’t escape the target directory
   * This preserves security guarantees while allowing valid use cases

3. **Optional configuration (fallback)**

   * Introduce a flag like `allowSafeSymlinks`
   * Default remains secure, but users can opt-in for controlled environments

### Goal

Maintain the security guarantees introduced by SECURITY-3657 while restoring compatibility for common development workflows that rely on symlinks.

Let me know if this direction sounds good, or if you’d prefer a stricter approach (e.g., always skipping symlinks during stash).

I can start with a PR once aligned.

The archive code does not pass `LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS` to `Dirscanner.Glob`, so it follows symlinks -- an option the security fix does not handle well.

comments.body:
> Declaring an entry to be a symlink and then collecting its children seems wrong.

It seems this is not (exactly) what's happening here though.

```
$ tar tvzf foo.tar.gz 
-rw-r--r-- 0/0              29 2026-04-24 09:25 top/sub/subsub/file
-rw-r--r-- 0/0              29 2026-04-24 09:25 top/sub2/file
```

The `stash` tar itself only collects files. The problem is the `unstash` over a non-empty directory, because we traversed symlinks to collect files, and now want to extract them again. This also means we have (potentially significantly) inflated stash sizes, since files are potentially collected N+1 times for N symlinks.

The following Pipeline reveals the directory layout before and (when cleaning to make the `unstash` pass) after:
```
node {
    sh 'rm -rf top/ ; mkdir -p top/sub top/sub2 ; ln -s ../sub2 top/sub/subsub ; date > top/sub2/file'
    sh 'find top/ -ls'
    stash includes: 'top/**', name: 'foo'
    sh 'rm -rf top/'
    unstash 'foo'
    sh 'find top/ -ls'
}
```

```

title: Fenced-in Admin
need_summary: Whether Jenkins “fenced-in Admin” rights could be safely delegated without allowing users to elevate themselves to Administer, with the answer anchored in JEP 223 and the Manage permission guidance.
security_topic: permission scoping to prevent privilege escalation
question_text: I would like to see the ability to grant Admin rights to a user, but fence them into specific categories of configuration. For example, on a shared Jenkins site you don't want to grant Admin rights to users and risk exposing projects others should not see. But that also prevents users from creating Cloud Nodes that use Docker images as slaves.
answer_text:
This is what Overall/Manage permission is for: https://www.jenkins.io/jep/223

Anything that cannot be used to elevate one's own permission to Administer should ultimately use Manage. The problem is that many features can be used in that way. If a feature you want them "fenced in" like that can be used to elevate permissions, it's not suitable.

          var refElement = document.getElementById("ecp_${h.escape(it.randomName)}_0");

                  height += refElement.offsetHeight + 3;
              }
          }
          else {
              height = maxCount * 25.5;
          }

          height = Math.floor(height);
          document.getElementById("ecp_${h.escape(it.randomName)}").style.height = height + "px";
      };

      f();
  })();

title: [JENKINS-75967] A single browser tab with queue widget can DoS a Jenkins controller
need_summary: Whether the browser-tab-driven queue widget DoS can be mitigated by bypassing WithThreadName, anchored on workflow-support-plugin PR #345 and the introduced config toggle.
security_topic: DoS from frequent queue widget auto-refresh and native thread-name calls
question_text: A single browser tab with queue widget can DoS a Jenkins controller
answer_text: PR https://github.com/jenkinsci/workflow-support-plugin/pull/345 was recently merged, allowing installations to bypass WithThreadName changes (hence callouts to native OS methods) which in our deployments happened thousands of times per second. Using the introduced toggle in local Jenkins config fixed the problem for us.
